BackstoryDef.title: Mountain terrace child
BackstoryDef.description: They grew crops on narrow terraces where a careless step could cost more than an entire harvest.

BackstoryDef.title: Vale forge apprentice
BackstoryDef.description: Their forge served mountain villages, producing tools and fittings needed in isolated communities.

BackstoryDef.title: Stone road laborer
BackstoryDef.description: They helped repair steep roads, retaining walls, and mountain paths leading toward the high castles of the Vale.

BackstoryDef.title: Sept carver's child
BackstoryDef.description: They learned to carve the Seven, falcons, moons, and intricate stonework for septs and noble halls.

BackstoryDef.title: Ward beneath the Eyrie
BackstoryDef.description: Raised among Vale nobility, they learned chivalry, courtesy, and the proud genealogies of mountain Houses.

BackstoryDef.title: Falcon House heir
BackstoryDef.description: Their tutors prepared them to inherit a mountain estate, its sworn swords, and its difficult highland tenants.

BackstoryDef.title: Second son of the Vale
BackstoryDef.description: With little land awaiting them, they sought distinction through horses, hunting, and the martial traditions of the Vale.

BackstoryDef.title: Stone bastard
BackstoryDef.description: Bearing the bastard name Stone taught them that even the most honorable courts possessed sharp edges.

BackstoryDef.title: Mountain goatherd
BackstoryDef.description: They guarded hardy goats on slopes where shadowcats and raiders could appear without warning.

BackstoryDef.title: Young Falcon page
BackstoryDef.description: They served knights famous for their chivalry and learned that polished armor still needed blood scrubbed from it.

BackstoryDef.title: High Vale farmer
BackstoryDef.description: They cultivated fertile valleys beneath mountains that isolated their community from much of Westeros.

BackstoryDef.title: Mountain armorer
BackstoryDef.description: They forged armor and climbing hardware for knights and soldiers accustomed to dangerous mountain roads.

BackstoryDef.title: Vale stonemason
BackstoryDef.description: Mountain castles and winding roads demanded builders who understood stone better than timber.

BackstoryDef.title: Falconer and huntsman
BackstoryDef.description: They trained hunting birds and accompanied nobles into the mountains in search of game.

BackstoryDef.title: Sept sculptor
BackstoryDef.description: Their statues and reliefs decorated septs, roadside shrines, and halls devoted to the Seven.

BackstoryDef.title: Mountain healer
BackstoryDef.description: Remote communities depended on them when the nearest maester was several dangerous roads away.

BackstoryDef.title: Vale chronicler
BackstoryDef.description: They recorded lineages, old battles, and the many claims of Houses proud of their Andal ancestry.

BackstoryDef.title: Knight of the Vale
BackstoryDef.description: Raised in one of Westeros's strongest traditions of knighthood, they are as comfortable in the saddle as on foot.

BackstoryDef.title: Mountain castellan
BackstoryDef.description: They managed supplies, servants, guards, and tenants for an isolated stronghold.

BackstoryDef.title: Falcon Court envoy
BackstoryDef.description: Their work required navigating the pride of Vale Houses without insulting men whose ancestors remembered every slight.
